items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was very happy about the opportunity of working for Benny because he was my favourite arranger and alto player... But I made the other rehearsals... myself on trumpets

ctx.x: We were on the stand that had been occupied by Fess Williams. I sat on the end on the right side of the stand, Frank Newton on my left and Dickie Wells left of Frank. Cecil stood in the middle, Lester Carr left of Cecil, Harold McFerran in the back, Mack Walker and Lloyd were on the same level as Don.

Rex Stewart was on the left side of the other bandstand and that put him and I next to each other. From the very first night until Horace finished at the end of February it was a battle of jazz which ended in a draw. Benny and Rex did a lot for Horace's orchestra. Benny played much more than I had heard him play with Charlie Johnson orchestra and Rex was the fastest man I had ever heard on trumpet. He was better than he was when I first saw him with Fletcher in Cincinnati and I especially liked his fast execution…

Each band would have what we called a killer- diller number to finish every set and as the dancers and listeners roared their approval, it was difficult for one band to start after the other had played their killer- diller. Both bands had their fans and there were always discussions amongst the dancers and the connoisseurs of jazz. Both sides were connoisseurs. The dancers heard everything that was happening on the band stand while they were still flying through the air, Lindy-Hopping.
